question: How much of the near-maximal AusTraits trait-order reconfiguration can be generated by finite-species uncertainty in the memory-loss rho estimator?

population.support_rule: retain systems with prune-only native tips >=40 so both split halves contain at least 20 native tips
population.system_membership: fixed before split-half rho results are computed

split.within_axis_rule: for each replicate independently permute tree tips with a deterministic seed and divide into two halves differing in size by at most one
split.effect: Spearman(all unordered within-half patristic distances, absolute log-state differences)
split.full_effect_check: recomputed full-tree rho must equal the frozen real-effect value to numerical tolerance

outputs.system_reliability: Spearman correlation of half-A versus half-B rho across systems for each replicate and axis
outputs.measurement_order_reversal: within each family and replicate, compare every non-tied pair of retained traits; count whether the trait order in half A disagrees with half B
outputs.observed_cross_family_reversal: on the identical high-support system set, compute the full-data cross-family trait-pair reversal probability

interpretation.measurement_much_lower: supports biological lineage-specific re-ordering beyond finite-species estimator instability
interpretation.measurement_similar: substantially weakens the biological re-wiring interpretation; describe observed reversal mainly as rank uncertainty
interpretation.measurement_higher: do not claim biological re-wiring from pair-order reversal

role: post-outcome exploratory reliability analysis; no prospective decision is reclassified
